_note: Copy to docs/work/checklist/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<subject>.json. Never fill this file in place. status is pass|fail|skipped|substituted; substituted means checked by a different instrument than the item names, and its reason must say which. accepted stays null until a human answers it, so an unfinished run is visibly unfinished. Delete any item whose feature no longer exists rather than skipping it.

derived.note: Produced by scripts/derive-facts.py at run time, never typed from memory or a previous run.

findings-against-prior-runs._example: Delete this example. One entry per thing an earlier run got wrong — a verdict, a reason, or a step that could not have failed. A checklist that can only describe the current build cannot report that the last checklist lied.

items.expected-result: Release build and pack succeed; the global ai-raccoon tool force-updates to this build and `ai-raccoon --version` matches derived.version
`serve --port 0` binds and reports its port; `serve --restart` on that port cycles the server it finds rather than attaching, and never touches port 7721
memory_write returns a hash for a stored entry; a rejected write returns Stored=false with a reason and no fabricated hash (ADR-0032)
memory_search returns the written entry through hybrid BM25 + vector RRF ranking
memory_get returns the full entry for a hash reachable from the caller; an unknown hash refuses rather than returning empty (ADR-0035)
a `file#section` query returns that exact chunk within the production result window

memory_write a note made of"The village fete committee met in the church hall to plan stalls, bunting, the tombola and the cake competition." forty-five times, space-joined (ten fit in one chunk since 1.56), then " Invoice reference vk83jq was filed with the parish council." Premise: sqlite shows more than one entries row for the note's path. memory_search {query: "vk83jq", kind: memory, minRelativeScore: 0} returns the note with an `fts` leg in evidenceByHash, and one of its rows holds `vk83jq` whole (`instr(value,'vk83jq')`). A vector-only hit does not count: the vector leg finds this note on a broken build too. Then write a note holding one whitespace-free term of about 2,500 characters (40 concatenated SHA-256 hex digests); premise: no row holds the whole term; searching the whole term returns that note with an `fts` leg. A build without ADR-0120 returns both notes by the vector leg only, and no row holds vk83jq (ADR-0120)

memory_write a note with sourceFile /notes/minutes.md made of 62 paragraphs separated by blank lines ("Paragraph N of the parish minutes records the treasurer's report on hall repairs, roof slates and the organ fund."), the first opening with "Opening marker zq71". Premise: sqlite shows more than one row for the note's path. memory_search {query: "zq71", kind: memory, minRelativeScore: 0} returns it with chunkIndex 0, and sqlite gives chunk_index 0 for the row where `instr(value,'zq71') > 0`. A build without ADR-0122 puts the opening at the last index (1 of 2 on 1.56.1) (ADR-0122)

On a fresh scratch bank with no engine set, memory_write four ordinary notes and one containing POISON-7Q, so all five rows are pending. Start `python3 scripts/poison-embedding-stub.py --port 0 --log stub.log`, then run `model embedding set openai stub-embed <printed base URL> --api-key stub-key` against the scratch server. memory_embed_pending returns {processed, pending} and does not fail or hang. Later calls return pending 1. `sqlite3 -readonly memory.db "SELECT embed_state, embed_attempts, count(*) FROM entries GROUP BY 1, 2"` shows four rows embedded and the poison row pending at embed_attempts 3. memory_stats.pending is 1, and the count of poison lines in stub.log stays the same across three more memory_embed_pending calls. Negative control: stub.log holds a `poison 5` batch line followed by `ok 1` lines, so the engine refused the batch and answered the single rows. A build without ADR-0119 fails every memory_embed_pending with ClientResultException, keeps all five rows pending and adds a poison line per call (ADR-0119)
each registered write-path policy rejects what it claims to, the write reports the rejection, and the rejected content is retrievable from the noise store (ADR-0039)
the refuse and annotate tiers behave as ADR-0040 describes; the structural detector is off until `queryguard structural enable` and only ever annotates (ADR-0041)

Copy the live bank with VACUUM INTO (clear its watches) and serve the copy. A memory_search for the first ~7,000 characters of CLAUDE.md, and one for ~7,000 characters of stopwords plus two content words, each return in seconds at vectorWeight 0, and data.warning says keyword matching is capped at the first 64 distinct words, with no clause saying it still sees the query in full. On a fresh bank with vectorWeight 0 and minRelativeScore 0, a marker word placed after 70 distinct filler words gets no hit, and the same word placed first gets an `fts` leg. Repeats do not use up the cap: the marker after 80 repeats of two words is still found. A 6-token query keeps the stopword `the`, and a 71-token query drops it. Negative control: install the release before the cap into a scratch --tool-path and run the same copy and queries. There the paste takes tens of seconds, the stopword run times out, and both the trailing marker and the 71-token `the` are found (ADR-0126)
memory_watch_status lists live registrations and their sync state

Watch a scratch directory (`settings ingest scope add`, `settings watch enable`, memory_watch_add) holding x.md, w.md and y.md, plus node_modules/pkg/index.md and .git/notes.md, each with a term found nowhere else. Wait for three watch_files rows, `chmod 000` node_modules, wait 2 s, then edit y.md so watches.last_change_ts moves past x.md's watch_files.updated_at. Read both values while the server runs, because a stopped WAL bank will not open read-only. Stop the server. Replace one word of x.md with a new term of the same byte length and `touch -t $(date -r <t> +%Y%m%d%H%M.%S)` it, where t is between x.md's updated_at and last_change_ts. Rewrite w.md at a different size with a new term, and touch it to before its own updated_at. Restart on the same data root. Within seconds memory_search finds both new terms, watch_files shows new updated_at and size for x.md and w.md, and memory_watch_status reads Healthy. Neither the node_modules term nor the .git term is ever found. Premise: before the restart, updated_at(x.md) <= mtime(x.md) <= last_change_ts. A build without ADR-0121 finds neither new term, because it re-queues only files with mtime > last_change_ts. The 5-minute heal pass (WatchHostedService.HealInterval, event 322 at Debug) is optional: it needs a server left up for over 5 minutes (ADR-0121)
memory_promotion_list reports propose-tier candidates and queue state accurately
